description: The SIDC, the Solar Physics Department of the Royal Observatory of Belgium, runs a space weather and space climate service centre that preserves long solar data series and monitors and forecasts solar activity around the clock. It has been the World Data Center for the sunspot index since 1981, continuing the work of the Zürich Observatory, and is responsible for calculating and preserving the International Sunspot Number. It became the ISES Regional Warning Centre Brussels in 2000 and publishes daily space weather reports and forecasts (URSIgrams), monthly and quarterly bulletins, real-time alerts for halo CMEs, large flares and quiet periods, and event catalogues of sunspot groups, flares, coronal holes and coronal mass ejections, with data from space instruments such as SWAP, LYRA and EUI and from ground imaging and radio. It hosts the coordination centre and service desk of the ESA Space Weather Service Network and is the central advisory hub, with STCE partners, of the PECASUS network that serves civil aviation. Access to the bulletins and data is free online; the site has a data policy and terms of use, and some services need an account. Caveats: the page read is an overview, and terms differ by product. Coverage is global solar activity, from Belgium. It supports hazard exposure analysis of space weather for power grids, satellites, aviation and GNSS; related records are the ESA Space Weather Service Network, the NICT space weather forecast and Space Weather Canada.
